stem: Which of these is an external parasite of cattle?

options.rationale: Correct: lives on the skin and sucks blood.
A roundworm living in the gut.
Lives in the liver.
Lives in the intestine.

explanation: Ticks live on the outside of the host; the others are internal parasites.

stem: Which disease is spread by the blue tick?

options.rationale: Correct: and gallsickness.
Spread by the bont tick.
Spread by the brown ear tick.
Spread by tsetse flies.

explanation: The blue tick, a one-host tick, transmits redwater (babesiosis) and gallsickness (anaplasmosis).

stem: What is meant by a one-host tick?

options.content: It feeds only on one species of animal
options.rationale: One-host refers to individuals, not species.

options.content: It needs only one blood meal in its life
options.rationale: Each stage feeds.

options.content: Only the adult female feeds on blood
options.rationale: Larvae and nymphs feed too.

options.content: All feeding stages stay on one animal
options.rationale: Correct.

explanation: Larva, nymph and adult all feed on the same individual animal; only the engorged female drops off.

stem: How many legs does the larva of a tick have?

options.rationale: That is the nymph and adult.
No tick stage has four legs.
No tick stage has ten legs.
Correct: nymphs and adults have eight.

explanation: Tick larvae have six legs; after moulting the nymph and adult have eight.

stem: Why are three-host ticks harder to control by dipping than one-host ticks?

options.content: They are too large for acaricides to kill
options.rationale: Size is not the reason.

options.content: They feed only in winter when dipping stops
options.rationale: They are most active in the wet season.

options.content: Much of their life is spent off the host
options.rationale: Correct: dipping reaches only stages on the animal.

options.content: They live inside the animal's gut
options.rationale: They are external parasites.

explanation: Each stage drops off to moult on the ground and can survive a long time on the veld, out of reach of dip.

stem: A pig has thick, crusty, hairless patches of skin and scratches constantly. Which parasite is most likely?

options.rationale: These attach inside cattle ears.
They bite and spread trypanosomes.
Correct: they burrow in the skin.
Internal parasites of the liver.

explanation: Mites cause mange: intense itching and thick, crusty skin.

stem: To save money, a farmer halves the amount of acaricide concentrate in his dip wash. What is the most serious long-term result?

options.content: The cattle will gain weight faster
options.rationale: More ticks means poorer growth.

options.content: The wash will become stronger over time
options.rationale: It stays weak.

options.content: Ticks may become resistant to the acaricide
options.rationale: Correct: survivors breed resistant ticks.

options.content: Ticks will move from the cattle to the goats only
options.rationale: Not a result of weak dip.

explanation: A weak wash lets the toughest ticks survive and breed, so resistance spreads and the acaricide stops working.
hints: Which ticks survive a weak dip?

stem: Why is tick grease applied to the ears and under the tail of cattle?

options.rationale: Not a purpose of tick grease.

options.content: Ticks hide there where dip may not reach
options.rationale: Correct: hand dressing covers missed sites.

options.content: It stops the cattle from drinking dip wash in the tank
options.rationale: Grease has no effect on drinking.

options.content: It makes the cattle grow longer hair
options.rationale: Not a purpose of tick grease.

explanation: Brown ear ticks and others attach in places that dip or spray may not wet thoroughly.
hints: Where do brown ear ticks attach?

explanation: False. Ticks are arachnids: nymphs and adults have eight legs. Insects such as lice and fleas have six.

stem: Match each tick with a disease it transmits.
explanation: Blue tick: redwater and gallsickness. Brown ear tick: theileriosis. Bont tick: heartwater.

stem: Complete the stages of a tick's life cycle.
explanation: Egg, larva (six legs), nymph (eight legs), adult.

stem: Name the general term for a chemical that kills ticks.
A dip tank holds 12,000 L. Assume the acaricide is used at 1.5 mL of concentrate per litre. How many litres of concentrate are needed to charge the tank?
explanation: 1.5 × 12,000 = 18,000 mL = 18 L. Forgetting to convert mL to L gives 18,000.
workedSolution: 1. 1.5 × 12,000 = 18,000 mL = 18 L. Forgetting to convert mL to L gives 18,000.

stem: A goat keeper mixes an acaricide spray at 2.5 mL per litre (assume) in a 20 L knapsack sprayer. How many mL of concentrate are needed?
Average tick counts fall from 150 to 30 per animal after a month of regular dipping. Calculate the percentage reduction.
explanation: (150 − 30) ÷ 150 × 100 = 80%. 20% is what remains, not the reduction.
workedSolution: 1. (150 − 30) ÷ 150 × 100 = 80%. 20% is what remains, not the reduction.

stem: Explain **two** ways in which ticks reduce the profits of a beef farmer.

points.description: Ticks suck blood, causing anaemia and irritation.
So cattle grow more slowly and reach market weight later / lose condition.
Ticks transmit diseases such as redwater, gallsickness and heartwater.
Which kill cattle or need costly treatment / bites damage hides, lowering their value.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Ticks suck blood and irritate cattle, so they grow slowly and fetch less. They also spread redwater and heartwater, which kill animals or need expensive treatment, and their bites leave holes that lower the value of hides.

hints: Think of blood, disease and hides.

stem: State **three** precautions to take when dipping cattle in a plunge dip.

points.description: Do not dip animals that are hot, tired or thirsty (water them first) / handle young calves so they do not swallow wash.
Keep the wash at the correct strength, replenished as instructed.
Wear protective clothing when handling concentrate / keep wash out of rivers and dams.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Water and rest the cattle before dipping so they do not drink the wash, keep the wash at the correct strength, and wear protective clothing when handling the concentrate and never let wash drain into a river.

hints: Think of the animals, the wash and the people.

stem:
Two herds near Masvingo graze similar veld. Herd A is dipped weekly and herd B monthly. Average ticks counted per animal on one side are shown.

| Month | Herd A: dipped weekly | Herd B: dipped monthly |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct | 22 | 25 |
| Nov | 35 | 64 |
| Dec | 41 | 118 |
| Jan | 38 | 152 |
| Feb | 30 | 140 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the mean tick count for herd B over the five months.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the percentage increase in herd B's tick count from October to January.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why tick numbers rise in both herds from October to January.

points.description: The hot, wet season (summer rains) favours egg hatching and survival of larvae.
Long, moist grass gives larvae places to wait for hosts / more ticks complete their life cycle.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why weekly dipping keeps blue tick numbers much lower than monthly dipping.

points.description: The blue tick stays on one host for about three weeks from larva to engorged female.
Weekly dipping kills ticks before the females drop off to lay eggs; with monthly dipping many females complete feeding and lay thousands of eggs.

parts.explanation: Dip interval shorter than the time on the host.

explanation: Interpret tick counts and link dipping interval to the one-host life cycle.

stem: Rudo's goats near Hwange have dull coats, rub against fences and have small, pale eggs glued to their hairs. One kid has a wound full of maggots.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the parasite whose eggs are glued to the hairs.
parts.explanation: **Lice**; their eggs (nits) are glued to hairs.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Which insect causes the maggots in the wound?

options.rationale: Tsetse suck blood; they do not cause maggots in wounds.
Correct: blowflies lay eggs in wounds (fly strike).
Fleas do not produce maggots in wounds.
Mosquito larvae live in water.

parts.explanation: Blowflies lay eggs on wounds and the maggots feed on the flesh.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe how Rudo should treat the wounded kid.

points.description: Restrain the kid calmly, remove the maggots and clean the wound (wearing gloves).
Apply an insecticidal wound dressing and keep checking until it heals.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Suggest **two** ways of controlling the lice in the whole herd.

points.description: Treat (spray, dip or dust) all the goats in the herd, repeating the treatment to kill lice that hatch later.
Clean the housing and bedding / improve feeding (lice are worse on animals in poor condition) / isolate and treat new goats.

explanation: Identify external parasites from signs and plan treatment.
hints: Which parasites glue their eggs to hairs?
